8-23-4 Note on SOM Replacement

SOM retains its memory (date/time/BIOS setting) by receiving 3V from coin battery on GFS Board. Therefore, when SOM and GFS boards are separated, SOM is likely to loose its date/time setting. In such case, follow the procedure outlined below to update BIOS information.
8-23-4-1 Configuring BIOS
1.) On bootup, press "DEL" to access BIOS.
2.) When password is prompted, enter "polaris" from AN Keyboard.
3.) After successfully entering BIOS, verify the following parameters.
Table 8-42 Configuring BIOS
4.) Change date/time parameters as needed, and save the changes.
5.) Select [Save & Exit] or [Exit] on the tab menu.
6.) Select [Restore Defaults] or [Load Setup Defaults].
NOTE: Following steps from 7.) to 13.) are only required for R4.2.5x.
7.) Select [Advanced] on the tab menu.
8.) Select [USB].
9.) Make sure that [USB Mass Storage Driver Support] value is [Disabled].
10.) Push ESC button.
11.) Select [Trusted Computing].
12.) Confirm [TPM20 Device Found] is displayed.
13.) Push ESC button once.
14.) Select [Save changes and Exit] or [Exit Saving Changes].
15.) Reboot the console.
8-23-4-2 Modifying contents of EEPROM (ComExpress VPD)
1.) Exit to Desktop (Refer to Section 7-3 "Exit to Windows Desktop" on page 7-5).
2.) Start VPD Editor by clicking icon on the desktop "vpdedit".
NOTE: For following steps, 8-23-5 "Note on EEPROM Replacement" on page 8-213 can be referred.
3.) Select "COMEXPRESS" from Device Grid (right pane).
4.) Select Part number (GE format) and click Pull-down menu.
5.) Select correct one for the installed ComExpress.
6.) Double Click value for "Serial Number" Type in COMEXPRESS serial number. Serial-number is described on the ComExpress Module itself.
7.) Click "Write Dirty Fields" button on right pane.
8.) Exit "vpdedit".

8-23-5 Note on EEPROM Replacement

NOTE: EEPROM on GFS contains VPD (Vital Product Data) for SOM (ComExpress). This VPD contains information such as system serial number to be matched to Software License Key, or Board revision number that is cross referenced to system software for compatibility.
Service personnel may require to initialize EEPROM or to modify EEPROM contents for proper operation of the system.
EEPROM on GFS Board
Figure 8-124 EEPROM on GFS Board
NOTE: There are various types of VPD integrated in the system.
* FuncRev = Functional Revision number that is separate from part Rev. System control software monitors board functional rev to verify compatibility.

8-23-5-2 Initializing EEPROM
When a new EEPROM is attached to a system, it will require initialization.
1.) Select "COMEXPRESS" from Device Grid (right pane).
2.) Select "Load Template" from right pane.

3.) For R1 and R2, select "ComexpMaster.VPD". For R3, select "ComexpMasterFuncRev3A.VPD". For R4 or later, select "ComexpMasterFuncRev5A.VPD". File is found under c:\Scanner\target\resources\acquisition\Housekeeping.

8-23-5-3 Modifying contents of EEPROM (ComExpress VPD)
System reads off Console Serial Number from EEPROM and match that against installed option string.
Therefore, without having correct serial number in EEPROM (ComExpress VPD).
1.) Exit to Windows Desktop (Refer to Section 7-3 "Exit to Windows Desktop" on page 7-5).
2.) Start VPD Editor by clicking icon on the desktop "vpdedit".
3.) Select "COMEXPRESS" from Device Grid (right pane).
4.) Double Click value for "System Serial Number".
5.) Type in consolefs serial number.
6.) Select Part number (GE format) and click Pull-down menu.
7.) Select correct one for the installed ComExpress.
8.) Double Click value for "Serial Number" type in COMEXPRESS serial number. Serial number is described on the ComExpress Module itself. It is NOT System Serial Number.
9.) Click "Write Dirty Fields" button on right pane.
10.) Exit "vpdedit".
Figure 8-133 COMEXPRESS

NOTE: This procedure can be applied to other components with VPD, for example, for modifying GFS FuncRev value. However, it is unlikely need for such event arises, as these VPD components are hardware-integrated into boards.
